questions.q: What is this passage mainly about?
options: How jet lag is diagnosed and treated in clinical settings
The definition, history and defining criteria of circadian rhythms
Why plants and animals sleep at different times of day
The genetics and treatment of human sleep disorders only
questions.explain: It defines circadian rhythms, traces their discovery, lists criteria, and discusses their origin.

questions.q: Which plant did Theophrastus' ancient account of leaves closing at night turn out to describe?
options: Rose
Mimosa
Tamarind
Fig
questions.explain: The tree he described was later identified as the tamarind tree.

questions.q: What did de Mairan's 1729 experiment show about Mimosa pudica?
options: Its leaf movements persisted even in constant darkness
Its leaves stopped moving whenever light was removed
Its leaf movements sped up sharply in cold weather
Its leaves opened only at noon in constant darkness
questions.explain: 24-hour leaf movement patterns persisted in constant darkness, suggesting an endogenous clock.

questions.q: What was distinctive about the people in the Utah family with the first human clock mutation?
options: They were extreme night owls with sleep delayed by four hours
They slept almost no hours but kept normal daily rhythms
They were extreme morning larks with sleep advanced by four hours
They had a 36-hour cycle and slept every second night
questions.explain: Affected individuals were extreme morning larks with 4-hour advanced sleep and other rhythms.

questions.q: What does the passage suggest about the purpose of circadian rhythms?
options: They only help organisms match the outside environment
They also coordinate internal metabolic processes
They are mainly a byproduct of temperature changes
They evolved once and spread to all kingdoms
questions.explain: Rhythms persisted for hundreds of generations of flies in constant conditions, suggesting internal regulation matters as much as environmental coordination.
